questions.title: Sphere falling in a liquid — vectors, units & upthrust

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: A vector quantity is a quantity that has magnitude and direction.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
D = 6πrηv, so η = D/(6πrv)
SI base units of D (a force) = kg m s⁻²; of r = m; of v = m s⁻¹
units of η = kg m s⁻² ÷ (m × m s⁻¹) = kg m⁻¹ s⁻¹

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
The sphere falls at constant velocity, so the resultant force on it is zero (equilibrium):
W = U + D (weight acts downwards; drag and upthrust act upwards)

questions.title: Child on a scooter — momentum, acceleration & braking

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Momentum is the product of the mass and the velocity (of an object).

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer:
average force = rate of change of momentum = mΔv/Δt
= 16 × 0.60 / 1.1 = 8.7 N

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.answer:
work done = force × distance
F = W/s = 250/18 = 14 N

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.answer: Draw a line starting at distance 0 at a positive, non-zero value of kinetic energy (the child already moves at 0.60 m s⁻¹, so KE = ½ × 16 × 0.60² ≈ 2.9 J). From distance 0 to x, a straight line of positive gradient (constant acceleration; KE = ½m(u² + 2as) increases linearly with distance). From x to x + 18 m, a straight horizontal line at a non-zero value, continuous with the first line (constant velocity → constant kinetic energy).

questions.title: Stress–strain graph — Young modulus, moments & tension

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer:
E = σ/ε = gradient of the linear part of the graph
e.g. at strain 0.5% (= 5.0×10⁻³), stress = 12×10⁷ Pa
E = 12×10⁷ / 5.0×10⁻³ = 2.4×10¹⁰ Pa

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer: Draw a cross (×) at the end of the straight-line portion of the graph — at (1.0% strain, 24×10⁷ Pa) — and label it Q.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: The resultant force on the object is zero (in all directions), and the resultant moment (torque) about any point is zero.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer:
Taking moments about A:
clockwise moments: 33 × (0.65/2) + 1.5 × (0.65 − 0.12) = 10.7 + 0.80 = 11.5 N m
anticlockwise moment: T sin 50° × (0.65/2)
11.5 = T × 0.766 × 0.325 → T = 11.5/0.249 = 46 N

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.answer: The stress doubles to 3.0×10⁷ Pa. This is well below the stress at the limit of proportionality (2.4×10⁸ Pa) and so also below the stress at the elastic limit E on Fig. 3.1 — the elastic limit is not reached, so the wire behaves elastically (it returns to its original length when unloaded).

questions.title: Stationary wave in a pipe — transverse & longitudinal waves

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: In a longitudinal wave, the oscillations (of the particles of the medium) are parallel to the direction of transfer of energy. In a transverse wave, the oscillations are perpendicular to the direction of transfer of energy.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: An antinode is formed at the open end of the pipe — draw the letter A at the open end of the pipe (position of maximum displacement).

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
For the stationary wave in a pipe closed at one end (fundamental): L = λ/4
λ = 4 × 4.5×10⁻² = 0.18 m
f = v/λ = 340/0.18 = 1900 Hz

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer: Moving the piston to the left increases the length of the air column, so to keep the same number of antinodes the node–antinode distance (λ/4) must be longer — the wavelength increases. Since the speed of sound is constant and f = v/λ, the frequency of the sound wave is lower.

questions.title: Household circuit — currents, p.d., power & efficiency

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Electric potential difference is the energy transferred per unit charge (from electrical to other forms of energy when charge passes through a component).

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: X is a heater.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer:
p.d. across the 170 Ω resistor = 230 − 6.0 = 224 V
current in it = 224/170 = 1.3 A
By Kirchhoff's first law (conservation of charge): I₁ = 7.0 − 1.3 = 5.7 A

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.answer:
p.d. across the 2.4 Ω resistor = I₁ × R = 5.7 × 2.4 = 13.7 V
By Kirchhoff's second law (conservation of energy):
V_X = 230 − 6.0 − 13.7 = 210 V

parts.label: (b)(vi)
parts.answer:
efficiency = useful power output / total power input × 100%
= 1200/(230 × 7.0) × 100% = 0.745 × 100%
= 75% (74% if the 3 s.f. value 1.20×10³ W from (v) is used)

parts.label: (b)(vii)
parts.answer: The current in the power supply decreases — removing the 170 Ω resistor leaves an open circuit in that branch, so the total resistance of the circuit increases; since the e.m.f. is constant, I = E/R decreases.

questions.title: Alpha decay of a nucleus — momentum & kinetic energy

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The mass of the α-particle is much greater than the mass of the β⁺ particle. Both particles are positively charged. The magnitude of the charge on the α-particle is twice the charge on the β⁺ particle (2e compared with +1e).

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
In α-decay the proton number decreases by 2 and the nucleon number decreases by 4: P (84, 216) → Q (82, 212).
Draw a cross (×) at (82, 212) on Fig. 6.1 and label it Q.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: Q (82, 212) decays to R (83, 212): the proton number increases by 1 with no change in nucleon number, so this is β⁻ decay. The particles emitted are a β⁻ particle (electron) and an (electron) antineutrino.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer:
Momentum is conserved. Before the decay, P's momentum lies entirely along its original path, so the momentum components perpendicular to that path balance:
m_Q v_Q sin 68° = m_α v_α sin θ (masses are proportional to nucleon number; u cancels)
212 × 1.3×10⁵ × sin 68° = 4 × 150×10⁵ × sin θ
sin θ = (212 × 1.3 × 0.927)/(4 × 150) = 0.426
θ = 25°
